profile.name: india_ftth_evening
profile.title: Urban Indian home on fibre (FTTH/GPON), evening, devices on Wi-Fi
profile.status: EMULATION calibrated to published measurements; not a measurement of a real line

plan.why: Jio Fiber and BSNL 100 Mbit/s plans are symmetric 100/100; ISPs provision slightly above plan (Airtel TRAI disclosure shows the cap above nominal)

buffers.why: Byte-limited FIFO at the bottleneck, 50 ms at plan rate (625 kB). Matches US fibre loaded-latency medians (+10 to +14 ms) with tails beyond +100 ms when the FIFO stays full; a BNG default queue limit of 100 ms of the shaped rate bounds it from above

wan.why: Metro FTTH idle RTT to an in-city CDN about 10 ms (TRAI-reported latency 5-17 ms for Jio, Airtel, ACT, BSNL); idle jitter about 1 ms (Jio, ACT); GPON upstream DBA wait 0.1-2 ms (ITU-T G.984); loss 0.00-0.07 % (TRAI) plus Gilbert-Elliott burst loss fitted to broadband-gateway traces (about 0.1 %)

evening_capacity.why: Fibre delivers 90-100 % of plan in the evening on average (Ofcom, ACCC, FCC, Opensignal India); occasional dips from shared GPON trees and aggregation load; level shares and hold times are an engineering estimate (low confidence on timing)

failover_4g.why: The realistic cause of a 100 -> 20 Mbit/s drop is failover to a 4G backup: India's median 4G download is about 19 Mbit/s; metro 4G adds RTT, jitter (5-15 ms) and loss (0.5-2 %); LTE modems buffer 200-500 ms. Switch-over is modelled as instant (hot standby)

wifi.why: Per-packet Wi-Fi hop delay: lognormal access delay (5 GHz median 1 ms one way, 2.4 GHz 2 ms), growth above 50 % airtime use. Latency spikes are modelled as stall episodes in time (interference bursts, retries, rate-adaptation collapse): Poisson arrivals, 1 per 30 s on 5 GHz and 1 per 10 s on 2.4 GHz, scaled up with neighbour busy time, Pareto length (10 ms minimum, alpha 1.5, 200 ms cap); every packet arriving during an episode waits for its end. Calibration target: a home is quieter than the large campus WLAN measured by Sui et al. (median 3 ms, p90 about 20 ms, p99 above 250 ms; 5 GHz 35 % lower than 2.4 GHz). Background scans while a client carries traffic use short adaptive dwells (2-4 off-channel visits of 20-40 ms, every 3 min on average). Phones add power-save wake delay. Scan and stall schedules come from a per-station random stream seeded per run, so every arm sees the same events at the same moments. Stall rates and lengths are an engineering estimate (low confidence)

tcp.why: Google and Akamai serve most downloads with BBR; Windows, Android, macOS and Linux clients use CUBIC

engine_cpu.why: Raspberry Pi 4 (Cortex-A72) single-thread speed is about 1/9-1/11 of a desktop x86 core (PassMark, Geekbench); this lab vCPU runs CPython at about half a desktop core, so the engine gets 20 % of one vCPU
